strategy.summary: Reproduce the Timedelta / float-ndarray overflow in pandas by building the buggy revision ebd40365c94b from source (Cython extension in timedeltas.pyx) and running the developer's new tests in pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_arithmetic.py; the overflow test should fail on buggy (saturated int64 max returned, no OutOfBoundsTimedelta raised) and pass once the _check_div_float_array fix is present.

system_packages: a C compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython are documented in README.md without a constraint; no version is pinned by the evidence, so the strategy chooses current releases compatible with the checked-out revision's build
Python version is not stated by the evidence (null), so the strategy uses whichever interpreter the revision's pyproject supports and does not invent a version

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_arithmetic.py -k 'test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow or test_td_div_ndarray_zero_or_nan_still_nat or test_td_div_ndarray_in_bounds' -v
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_arithmetic.py::test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow (parametrized over unit in s, ms, us, ns and dtype in f8, f4), with other=np.array([1e-30]) asserting OutOfBoundsTimedelta('Overflow in timedelta division') for both td / other and td // other
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision ebd40365c94b, test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow fails for every unit/dtype combination because td / other returns an int64-max timedelta array instead of raising pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta); on the fixed revision the same parametrizations pass, and the zero/nan and in-bounds guard tests pass on both revisions.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timedelta(4, 'ns') / np.array([1e-30]) with float64 divisor: quotient 4e30 exceeds 2**63 and must raise on fixed code; float32 divisor is checked in float64 so it also raises.
risks: Buggy and fixed revisions differ in pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.pyx, so the Cython extension must be rebuilt after checkout; running tests against a stale build will not show the transition.

The passages do not give a NumPy version or Python version; a NumPy 2.x vs 1.x difference in float-to-timedelta casting could change whether the saturation occurs, so the strategy relies on the environment default and this is not verified.

The zero-divisor test emits a numpy divide RuntimeWarning unless np.errstate is used; the test already wraps it, but pytest warning filters configured to error could turn warnings into failures on either revision.

Behaviour depends on IEEE float64 arithmetic on a standard x86_64 or aarch64 platform; no architecture-specific or sanitizer-specific behaviour is stated, so none is assumed, but a platform where float-to-int64 casting of out-of-range values behaves differently would not transition as described.
Tz-aware DatetimeArray._add_offset fast path is explicitly out of scope and not exercised by these tests.

oracle.reference_source: pandas TimedeltaIndex behaviour and the developer's pytest.raises assertion in test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow
oracle.why: The test asserts a raised exception with a specific message, so the pass/fail transition is exact rather than numerical.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On ebd40365c94b, td / np.array([1e-30]) returns an int64-saturated timedelta array rather than raising, so pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta) reports no exception raised and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the _check_div_float_array check in timedeltas.pyx, the out-of-range quotient raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta with the matching message for both / and //, so the test passes.
